title: T1 fingerprint omits health in_breach + healthy_streak despite the 'covers ALL sim state' claim
evidence:
+	h := &state.health
+	w_i32(&w, h.meter_pct)
+	w_i32(&w, h.grace_ticks_left)
+	w_bool(&w, h.in_grace)
+	w_bool(&w, h.won)
+	w_bool(&w, h.lost)
+	w_u64(&w, h.surge_delivered)
+	w_u64(&w, h.surge_dropped)
+	w_bool(&w, h.prev_in_surge)
detail: Health_Meter also carries in_breach (hysteresis band) and healthy_streak (refill gate) per the health.odin hunk; neither is serialized. The header claims the fingerprint covers ALL sim state; band/streak divergence escapes per-tick hash detection.
recommended_fix: Serialize in_breach and healthy_streak in state_writer next to the other Health_Meter fields.

title: Comment claims 'Run_Lost supersedes everything' but a same-tick win suppresses the loss
evidence:
+	// lose: meter empty -> Error 404 (Run_Lost supersedes everything, E17)
+	if h.meter_pct <= 0 && !h.won && !h.lost {
detail: The win check runs first and sets h.won; the lose guard then skips on !h.won. When the surge ends and the meter empties on the same tick, the code gives Run_Won precedence — the opposite of the E17 comment.
recommended_fix: Decide the precedence: evaluate meter-empty before the surge-end win if loss supersedes, or correct the comment.

title: catalog_error_string uses %r, not a valid Odin fmt verb — the field name prints as fmt error noise
evidence: +	return fmt.aprintf("catalog %s: field %r — %s", err.file, err.field, err.rule, allocator = allocator)
detail: Odin fmt has no %r verb; the call renders the field as %!r(string=...). ODN-5's fail-fast 'named error' (which file, which field, what rule) is mangled exactly where load failures are diagnosed.

title: E28 asymmetry: the no-terminal path drops demand silently; the unroutable path emits per-packet drop events
evidence:
+		if len(src_ids) == 0 || len(dst_ids) == 0 {
+			// E28: undelivered demand feeds strain exactly like a loss
+			report.unmet += volume
+			report.dropped += volume
+			acc.demand_seen += u64(volume)
+			acc.dropped += u64(volume)
+			f.tick_drop[entry.class] += volume
+			continue
+		}
detail: Same E28 contract, two emission behaviors: this branch emits no Ev_Packet_Dropped, while the route_len==0 branch emits one per packet. Event-stream goldens and harness assertions see only one path.
recommended_fix: Emit Ev_Packet_Dropped{.Unreachable} (or a documented aggregate event) for the no-terminal accrual too.

title: surge_active is cleared by whichever set piece resolves first, even if another is still active
detail: One boolean tracks a list of set pieces; overlapping surges leave the flag false during the later one (snapshot surge_ends_in is likewise last-wins). The PROTO catalog has one surge, so latent.
recommended_fix: Derive surge_active from the set of active set pieces instead of clearing it on the first resolve.

title: demand_weight is parsed on packet types and demand entries but spawn weighting hardcodes 1
evidence: +			append(weights, 1) // demand_weight is uniform in the PROTO roster
detail: catalog.odin loads pt.demand_weight and de.demand_weight; neither is read anywhere in the diff. Dead catalog surface that survives validation and invites silent misconfiguration.
recommended_fix: Wire demand_weight into terminals_of/effective_volume, or drop the fields from the PROTO schema.

title: Comment pins the apply_tick convention to replay_test.odin — no such file appears in this diff
evidence: +	// boundary. THE CONVENTION IS PINNED by replay_test.odin (Perkins r1 on
detail: The diff adds only core non-test files; the cited pin file is not among them. A convention whose cited pin cannot be located in the reviewed change is unverifiable from it.
recommended_fix: Point the comment at the actual replay-equality test file.

title: Tautological comment: 'for edge i the entry node is the entry node'
evidence:
+			// The route walk tracks the node it came from; recompute quickly:
+			// for edge i the entry node is the entry node.
detail: Placeholder text in a subtle orientation walk (frac flip when traversing b->a). Explains nothing; the actual invariant lives in route_entry_node below.
recommended_fix: Replace with the real invariant: entry node of edge i = src walked through completed edges 0..i-1.

title: topology_apply_all/topology_clone have no production caller in this diff — step() applies commands individually
evidence: +topology_apply_all :: proc(t: ^Topology, cmds: []Command, cat: ^Catalogs, budget: i32, tick: u64, scratch := context.temp_allocator) -> (new_budget: i32, err: Edit_Error) {
detail: run.step deliberately loops topology_apply_edit per command (the comment explains why), so the E23 batch authority ships with no in-diff production caller. Two application paths that must never drift.
recommended_fix: Fine if tests/tooling call it — otherwise remove, or route replay batches through it.

title: growth_pool/forecasted/triggered/resolved serialize with no length prefix, unlike every other array
detail: The stated canonical rule is lengths-not-capacities; these four arrays write no length at all (nodes/pipes/packets/sla/rr/events all do), leaving the byte form ambiguous to any future reader.
recommended_fix: Write element counts before each of these arrays.
